title.en: Volume 101 Biographies 26: Xiao Yuyu and nephew Jun, Guan and son Song, Song and son: Hua, Song grandson: Fu, Hua and grandson: Mian, Hua and son: Fang, Fang's son; Lin, Fuceng and grandson: Gou
title.raw: 卷一百零一 列傳第二十六 蕭瑀瑀從子:鈞 瓘子:嵩 嵩子:華 嵩孫:復 華孫:俛 華孫:倣 倣子:廩 復曾孫:遘 Volume 101 Biographies 26: Xiao Yuyu and nephew Jun, Guan and son Song, Song and son: Hua, Song grandson: Fu, Hua and grandson: Mian, Hua and son: Fang, Fang's son; Lin, Fuceng and grandson: Gou

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀瑀從子:鈞 鈞兄子:嗣業 瓘子:嵩 嵩子:華 嵩孫:復 華孫:俛 華孫:倣 倣子:廩 復曾孫:遘 瑀曾孫:定

translations.literal: Xiao Yu; Yu's nephew's son: Jun; Jun's elder brother's son: Siye; Guan's son: Song; Song's son: Hua; Song's grandson: Fu; Hua's grandson: Mian; Hua's grandson: Fang; Fang's son: Lin; Fu's great-grandson: Gou; Yu's great-grandson: Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu; his nephew's son Jun; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Guan's son Song; Song's son Hua; Song's grandson Fu; Hua's grandsons Mian and Fang; Fang's son Lin; Fu's great-grandson Gou; and Yu's great-grandson Ding.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀，字時文，後樑明帝子也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, style name Shiwen, was a son of Emperor Ming of Later Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, whose style name was Shiwen, was a son of Emperor Ming of the Later Liang.

sentences.zh: 九歲，封新安王。

translations.literal: At nine years of age, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of nine he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 國除，以女兄為隋晉王妃，故入長安。

translations.literal: When his state was abolished, because his elder sister became consort of the Prince of Jin of Sui, he therefore entered Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After his principality was abolished, his elder sister having become consort to the Sui Prince of Jin, he went to live in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 瑀愛經術，善屬文。

translations.literal: Yu loved the classics and was skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was devoted to the classics and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 性鯁急，鄙遠浮華。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and impatient, and he despised and kept aloof from empty show.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and quick-tempered by nature, and held empty display in contempt.

sentences.zh: 嘗以劉孝標《辯命論》詭悖不經，乃著論非之，以為：「人稟天地而生而謂之命，至吉凶禍福則系諸人。

translations.literal: Once, holding that Liu Xiaobiao's 'Discourse on Fate' was perverse and contrary to the classics, he wrote a treatise to refute it, arguing: 'Man receives life from Heaven and Earth and this is called fate; but when it comes to good and ill fortune, blessing and disaster, these depend on the person.'
translations.idiomatic: He once judged Liu Xiaobiao's Discourse on Fate perverse and unorthodox, and wrote a refutation arguing that while life received from Heaven and Earth may be called fate, fortune and misfortune depend on the person.

sentences.zh: 今一於命，非先王所以教人者。

translations.literal: Now to make everything depend on fate is not what the former kings used to teach people.
translations.idiomatic: To reduce everything to fate is not how the ancient kings taught their subjects.

sentences.zh: 」通儒柳顧言、諸葛潁歎曰：「是足針孝標膏肓矣！」

translations.literal: The thorough scholars Liu Guyuan and Zhuge Ying exclaimed: 'This is enough to needle Xiaobiao in his vital spot!'
translations.idiomatic: The eminent scholars Liu Guyuan and Zhuge Ying marveled, "This strikes at the very heart of Xiaobiao's argument!"

sentences.zh: 晉王為太子，授右千牛。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became heir apparent, Yu was appointed Right Thousand-Bull.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin was made crown prince, Yu was appointed Right Thousand-Bull.

sentences.zh: 即帝位，妃為後，而瑀浸親寵，頻遷尚衣奉禦、檢校左翊衛鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, the consort became empress, and Yu gradually gained intimate favor, being repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe, and Acting Eagle-Brand Commandant of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession the consort became empress, and Yu grew ever closer in the emperor's favor, rising in turn to Attendant of the Imperial Wardrobe and acting Eagle-Brand commandant of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 感末疾，不呼醫，曰：「天若假吾餘年，因得為遁階矣！

translations.literal: Stricken with a lingering illness, he would not summon physicians, saying: 'If Heaven grants me a few more years, I may yet obtain the rank of recluse!'
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill with a chronic disease he refused to call a doctor, saying, "If Heaven grants me a few more years, I may yet take the path of withdrawal from the world!"

sentences.zh: 」後聞，責謂曰：「爾亡國後不安小官，而高為怪語，罪不測。

translations.literal: When the empress heard of this, she rebuked him, saying: 'After the fall of your state you were not content with a minor post, yet you utter lofty and strange words—the penalty is incalculable.'
translations.idiomatic: When the empress heard of it she rebuked him: "After your kingdom fell you were discontent with a modest office, and now you speak in lofty and strange terms—your offense is beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 」瑀復治疾，良已。

translations.literal: Yu then resumed treatment and recovered fully.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then resumed medical treatment and made a full recovery.

sentences.zh: 拜內史侍郎，數言事忤旨，稍見忌。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat; he often spoke on affairs contrary to the emperor's intent and gradually came to be regarded with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed vice minister of the Secretariat, he often spoke against the emperor's wishes and gradually fell under suspicion.

sentences.zh: 帝至雁門，為突厥所圍，瑀謀曰：「夷俗，可賀敦與兵馬事，況義成公主以帝女為之。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Yanmen and was besieged by the Turks, Yu proposed: 'By barbarian custom, the Khatun shares authority over troops and horses; moreover Princess Yicheng, being the emperor's daughter, holds that position.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Yanmen and was besieged by the Turks, Yu advised, "By nomad custom the khatun shares authority over troops and horses—and Princess Yicheng, the emperor's own daughter, holds that title."

sentences.zh: 若走一介使鐫喻，宜不戰而解。

translations.literal: If we send a single envoy to persuade her, the siege should be lifted without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: If we send a lone envoy to persuade her, the siege ought to lift without a battle.

sentences.zh: 又眾商陛下已平突厥，方復事遼東，故怠不肯戰。

translations.literal: Moreover the masses believe Your Majesty has already pacified the Turks and will next campaign against Liaodong, so they are slack and unwilling to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The troops also believe Your Majesty has already pacified the Turks and will next turn to Liaodong, so they are slack and unwilling to fight.

sentences.zh: 願下詔赦高麗，專討突厥，則人自奮矣。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty issue an edict pardoning Goguryeo and concentrating on chastising the Turks; then the men will rouse themselves of their own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict pardoning Goguryeo and concentrating on the Turks alone, and the men will rouse themselves.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 既而主詭辭謂突厥，果解圍去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the princess spoke deceitfully to the Turks, and the siege was indeed lifted and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The princess then spoke to the Turks in misleading terms, and the siege was indeed lifted.

sentences.zh: 然帝素意伐遼，又銜瑀以謀擫其機，謂群臣曰：「突厥何能為，瑀乘未解時乃紿恐我！

translations.literal: Yet the emperor had long intended to campaign against Liaodong, and he also resented Yu for a plan that thwarted his design; he told the ministers: 'What could the Turks do? Yu, while the siege was not yet lifted, deceived and frightened me!'
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor had long meant to campaign against Liaodong, and he resented Yu for thwarting his plans; he told the ministers, "What could the Turks do? Yu deceived and frightened me while the siege was still on!"

sentences.zh: 」遂出瑀為河池郡守。

translations.literal: He then sent Yu out as prefect of Hechi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Yu out as prefect of Hechi.

sentences.zh: 部有鈔賊萬人，吏不制，瑀募勇敢士擊降之，悉捐貲畜賜有功。

translations.literal: In his district there were ten thousand bandits whom the officials could not control; Yu recruited brave men to attack and subdue them, and donated all his property and livestock to reward those who had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand bandits in his district defied the officials; Yu recruited brave men, defeated and pacified them, and gave all his wealth and livestock to reward the meritorious.

sentences.zh: 又擊走薛舉眾數萬。

translations.literal: He also routed tens of thousands of Xue Ju's followers.
translations.idiomatic: He also routed tens of thousands of men under Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 是歲，州置七職，秦王為雍州牧，以瑀為州都督。

translations.literal: That year the prefecture was given seven offices; the Prince of Qin became governor of Yongzhou, and Yu was made regional commander of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That year the prefecture was given seven offices; the Prince of Qin became governor of Yongzhou and Yu was made regional commander.

sentences.zh: 詔嘗下中書，未即行，帝讓其稽，瑀曰：「隋季內史詔敕多違舛，百司不知所承。

translations.literal: An edict once came down to the Secretariat but was not immediately promulgated; the emperor reproached the delay, and Yu said: 'In the Sui era the Secretariat's edicts and orders were often erroneous, and the hundred offices did not know what to follow.'
translations.idiomatic: When an edict reached the Secretariat but was not promptly issued, the emperor reproached the delay; Yu replied, "Under the Sui the Secretariat's edicts were often wrong, and the offices did not know which to follow."

sentences.zh: 今朝廷初基，所以安危者系號令。

translations.literal: Now that the court is newly founded, what secures safety or peril hangs on commands.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the court is newly established, safety and peril hang on the clarity of commands.

sentences.zh: 比承一詔，必覆審，使先後不謬，始得下，此所以稽留也。

translations.literal: Whenever we receive an edict, we must review it again so that sequence is not confused before it may be issued—this is why there is delay.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever we receive an edict we review it again so that nothing is out of order before it is issued—that is why there is delay.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「若爾，朕何憂乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'If it is so, what have I to worry about?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If that is so, what have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 」初，瑀關內田宅悉賜勳家，至是，還給之。

translations.literal: Earlier, all of Yu's lands and houses within the passes had been granted to meritorious families; at this time they were returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier all of Yu's lands and houses within the passes had been granted to meritorious families; now they were restored to him.

sentences.zh: 瑀盡以分宗族，獨留廟室奉祠。

translations.literal: Yu gave it all away to his clansmen, keeping only the ancestral hall for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Yu distributed it all among his clansmen, keeping only the ancestral hall for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 王世充平，進尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was pacified, he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shichong was defeated he was promoted to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，以熒惑犯右執法，避位，不許。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because Mars invaded the Right Enforcer star, he resigned his post; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Mars crossed the Right Enforcer, he asked to resign; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷左僕射。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was transferred to left vice director.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，房玄齡、杜如晦新得君，事任稍分，瑀不能無少望，乘罅切詆，辭旨疏躁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had newly won the ruler's trust and their duties were somewhat divided; Yu could not be without some disappointment, and seizing openings he sharply denounced them, his words coarse and rash.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had newly won the emperor's trust and their duties were divided; Yu could not help some disappointment, and seizing every opening he attacked them in harsh and rash language.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，廢於家。

translations.literal: Taizong was angry and dismissed him to his home.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was angry and dismissed him to his home.

sentences.zh: 俄拜特進、太子少師，復為左僕射，實封六百戶。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Special Advancement and Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, again made Left Vice Director, with a substantive fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed special advancement and junior tutor to the heir apparent, again made left vice director, with a substantive fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 帝問瑀：「朕欲長保社稷，奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Yu: 'I wish to preserve the altars of state for long—how should I do it?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Yu, "I wish to preserve the realm for the long term—how should I do it?"

sentences.zh: 」瑀曰：「三代有天下所以能長久者，類封建諸侯以為籓屏。

translations.literal: Yu said: 'The reason the Three Dynasties could hold the realm for long was that they broadly enfeoffed feudal lords as screens and shields.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "The Three Dynasties endured because they broadly enfeoffed feudal lords as a protective screen around the throne."

sentences.zh: 秦置守令，二世而絕。

translations.literal: Qin appointed prefects and magistrates and perished in the second generation.
translations.idiomatic: Qin appointed prefects and magistrates and fell in the second generation.

sentences.zh: 漢分王子弟，享國四百年。

translations.literal: Han divided fiefs among the king's sons and younger brothers and held the realm for four hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Han divided fiefs among the imperial princes and held the realm for four hundred years.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉廢之，亡不旋跬。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin abolished it and fell in no time.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin abolished enfeoffment and fell almost at once.

sentences.zh: 此封建之有明效也。

translations.literal: This shows the clear efficacy of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: This shows how clearly enfeoffment served its purpose.

sentences.zh: 」帝納之，始議封建。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this and began to deliberate on enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and began to debate enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 坐與陳叔達忿爭御前不恭，免。

translations.literal: Because he quarreled angrily with Chen Shuda before the throne in disrespect, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled angrily with Chen Shuda before the throne in disrespect and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起為晉州都督。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was recalled as regional commander of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was recalled as regional commander of Jin.

sentences.zh: 入拜太常卿，遷御史大夫，參預朝政。

translations.literal: On entering court he was appointed Minister of Rites, then transferred to Censor-in-Chief and took part in deliberating government.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court he was made minister of rites, then censor-in-chief, and took part in government deliberations.

sentences.zh: 瑀諭議明辯，然不能容人短，意或偏駁不通，而向法深，房玄齡、魏征、溫彥博頗裁正之，其言多黜，瑀亦不平。

translations.literal: Yu was clear and sharp in exposition and debate, yet could not tolerate others' faults; his views were sometimes partial and contrary, and he inclined toward severity in law; Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Wen Yanbo often corrected him, and many of his statements were rejected—Yu was also resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was lucid and forceful in debate, yet could not abide others' faults; his views were sometimes partial and he inclined toward harsh law; Fang Xuanling, Wei Zheng, and Wen Yanbo often overruled him, and Yu grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 會玄齡等小過失，瑀即痛劾，不報，由是自失，罷為太子少傅，加特進，復為太常卿。

translations.literal: When Fang Xuanling and others had minor faults, Yu at once impeached them harshly; no response came, and from this he lost standing himself; he was dismissed as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, given Special Advancement, and again made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang Xuanling and others committed minor faults Yu impeached them harshly; the emperor did not act, and Yu thereby lost standing; he was made junior tutor to the heir apparent with special advancement, then again minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 拜河南道巡省大使。

translations.literal: He was appointed touring commissioner of Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed touring commissioner of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 九年，復參預政事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he again took part in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he again took part in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰：「武德季，太上皇有廢立議，顧朕挾不賞之功，于昆弟弗見容，瑀于爾時不可以利怵死懼，社稷臣也。

translations.literal: The emperor once said: 'Late in Wude, the retired emperor had deliberations on deposing and establishing; considering that I held unmatchable merit yet was not tolerated among my brothers, Yu at that time could not be swayed by profit or cowed by fear of death—he was a minister of the altars of state.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "Late in the Wude era the retired emperor debated deposing and establishing heirs; though I held unmatched merit my brothers would not tolerate me—yet Yu then could not be bought by profit or cowed by fear of death. He was a true minister of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」因賜詩曰：「疾風知勁草，版蕩識誠臣。

translations.literal: He therefore bestowed a poem saying: 'A fierce wind reveals the tough grass; turmoil reveals the loyal minister.'
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed a poem: "Only in a fierce wind do we know the tough grass; only in turmoil do we know the loyal minister."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「公守道耿介，古無以過，然善惡太明，或有時而失。

translations.literal: He also said: 'You uphold the Way with unbending integrity, unmatched since antiquity, yet you distinguish good and evil too sharply and sometimes err thereby.'
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "You uphold the Way with unbending integrity unmatched since antiquity, yet you distinguish good and evil too sharply and sometimes err thereby."

sentences.zh: 」瑀頓首謝曰：「既蒙教，又許以忠亮，雖死日，猶生年也。

translations.literal: Yu bowed his head and thanked him, saying: 'Having received instruction and also been acknowledged as loyal and upright, even the day of my death is like a year of life.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu bowed and thanked him: "Having received your instruction and been acknowledged as loyal and upright, even the day of my death is as a year of life."

sentences.zh: 」魏征曰：「臣有逆眾持法，主恕之以公；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: 'A subject who opposes the multitude to uphold the law—the ruler forgives him for his impartiality;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "A subject who opposes the multitude to uphold the law—the ruler forgives him for his impartiality;

sentences.zh: 孤特守節，主恕之以介。

translations.literal: one who stands alone guarding integrity—the ruler forgives him for his uprightness.'
translations.idiomatic: one who stands alone guarding integrity—the ruler forgives him for his uprightness."

sentences.zh: 昔聞其言，乃今見之。

translations.literal: I heard these words before; now I see them realized.
translations.idiomatic: I had heard these words before; now I see them realized.

sentences.zh: 使瑀不遇陛下，庸能自保邪？

translations.literal: Had Yu not met Your Majesty, how could he have preserved himself?
translations.idiomatic: Had Yu not met Your Majesty, how could he have preserved himself?

sentences.zh: 」晉王為皇太子，拜太子太保、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became heir apparent, Yu was appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, Yu was appointed grand tutor to the heir apparent and associate grand councilor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「三師，以德導太子者也，禮不尊，則無所取法。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'The three tutors guide the heir by virtue; if ritual does not honor them, there is nothing for him to take as model.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The three tutors guide the heir by virtue; if ritual does not honor them, the heir has no model to follow."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔：「師入謁，太子出門迎拜，師答拜；

translations.literal: An edict was then issued: 'When the tutor enters for audience, the heir shall go out the gate to welcome and bow; the tutor returns the bow;
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "When the tutor arrives, the heir shall go out to welcome him and bow; the tutor shall return the bow;

sentences.zh: 每門，讓乃入；

translations.literal: at each gate he shall yield before entering;
translations.idiomatic: at each gate the heir shall yield before the tutor enters;

sentences.zh: 師坐，然後坐；

translations.literal: when the tutor sits, then he may sit;
translations.idiomatic: the heir may sit only after the tutor is seated;

sentences.zh: 書前後著名，稱惶恐。

translations.literal: in letters he shall sign his name at beginning and end and style himself 'in trepidation.'
translations.idiomatic: in correspondence he shall sign his name and style himself 'in trepidation.'

sentences.zh: 」瑀素貴，但中狹。

translations.literal: Yu had long been eminent, but was narrow at heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had long been eminent, but was petty at heart.

sentences.zh: 每燕見，輒言：「玄齡輩朋黨盜權，若膠固然，特未反耳。

translations.literal: At every informal audience he would say: 'Fang Xuanling and his clique form a faction and steal power; they stick like glue—only they have not yet rebelled.'
translations.idiomatic: At every informal audience he would say, "Fang Xuanling and his clique form a faction and steal power—they stick like glue and have only not yet rebelled."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「知臣莫若君。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'No one knows his ministers like the ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "No one knows his ministers like the ruler."

sentences.zh: 朕雖不明，甯頓懵臧否？

translations.literal: Though I am not enlightened, would I suddenly be confused about who is worthy and who is not?
translations.idiomatic: Though I am not enlightened, would I suddenly be confused about who is worthy and who is not?

sentences.zh: 」因為瑀曉解，瑀以帝有所偏信，帝積久亦不平。

translations.literal: He then explained this to Yu to enlighten him; Yu believed the emperor was partial in his trust, and over time the emperor also grew resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He then explained this to enlighten Yu, but Yu believed the emperor was partial; over time the emperor grew resentful as well.

sentences.zh: 瑀好浮屠法，間請舍家為桑門，帝許之矣，復奏自度不能為，又足疾不入謁，帝曰：「瑀豈不得其所邪？

translations.literal: Yu loved Buddhist teachings and from time to time asked to leave his household and become a monk; the emperor consented, but Yu then memorialized that he judged himself unable to do it; he also had foot ailment and did not attend audience; the emperor said: 'Has Yu not found his proper place?'
translations.idiomatic: Yu loved Buddhism and from time to time asked to leave his household and become a monk; the emperor consented, but Yu then said he could not; he also had a foot ailment and stopped attending court; the emperor said, "Has Yu not found his proper place?"

sentences.zh: 」乃詔奪爵，下除商州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict was issued stripping his noble rank and demoting him to prefect of Shangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped his noble rank and demoted him to prefect of Shang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復其封，加特進。

translations.literal: Before long his fief was restored and he was given Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his fief was restored and he was given special advancement.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 遺命斂以單衣，無卜日。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be enshrouded in a single garment and not to choose an auspicious day.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to be buried in a single garment without choosing an auspicious day.

sentences.zh: 詔贈司空、荊州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Minister of Works and regional commander of Jingzhou, with burial at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him minister of works and regional commander of Jing, with burial at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 太常諡曰肅，帝以其性忌，改諡貞褊。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites gave the posthumous name Su; because of his jealous nature the emperor changed it to Zhenbian.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites proposed the posthumous name Su; because of his jealous nature the emperor changed it to Zhenbian (Upright but Narrow).

sentences.zh: 子銳，尚襄城公主，為太常少卿。

translations.literal: His son Rui married Princess Xiangcheng and served as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui married Princess Xiangcheng and served as vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 瑀從子 鈞

translations.literal: Yu's nephew's son Jun
translations.idiomatic: Yu's nephew's son Jun

sentences.zh: 鈞，瑀從子，有才譽。

translations.literal: Jun, Yu's nephew's son, had talent and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, Yu's nephew's son, was talented and well regarded.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，累遷諫議大夫、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: During Yonghui he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrating Censor and academician of the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era he rose to remonstrating censor and academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 左武候屬盧文操跳堞盜庫財，高宗以其職主干，當自盜罪死。

translations.literal: Lu Wencao, an attendant of the Left Martial Guard, scaled the wall and stole treasury goods; Gaozong, because his office was in charge, held that he should be guilty of self-theft and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wencao, an attendant of the Left Martial Guard, scaled the wall and stole from the treasury; Gaozong held that because his office was in charge he was guilty of self-theft and should die.

sentences.zh: 鈞曰：「囚罪誠死，然恐天下聞，謂陛下重貸輕法，任喜怒殺人。

translations.literal: Jun said: 'The prisoner indeed deserves death, yet I fear that when the realm hears of it they will say Your Majesty values goods over law and kills at whim according to pleasure or anger.'
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "The prisoner indeed deserves death, yet I fear the realm will say Your Majesty values goods over law and kills according to whim."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「真諫議也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'A true remonstrating censor!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "A true remonstrating censor!"

sentences.zh: 」詔原死。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned him from death.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him from death.

sentences.zh: 太常工為宮人通訊遺，詔殺之，且附律。

translations.literal: A craftsman of the Ministry of Rites conveyed messages and gifts for palace women; an edict ordered his execution and application of the statute.
translations.idiomatic: A craftsman of the Ministry of Rites carried messages and gifts for palace women; an edict ordered his execution under the applicable statute.

sentences.zh: 鈞言：「禁當有漸，雖附律，工不應死。

translations.literal: Jun said: 'Prohibitions should be gradual; though the statute applies, the craftsman should not die.'
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Prohibitions should be introduced gradually; though the statute applies, the craftsman should not die."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「如姬竊符，朕以為戒，今不濫工死，然喜得忠言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'When Ruji stole the tally I took it as a warning; now I will not put the craftsman to death without cause, yet I am glad to receive loyal counsel.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Ruji stole the tally I took it as a warning; I will not put the craftsman to death without cause, yet I am glad to receive loyal counsel."

sentences.zh: 」即宥工，徙遠裔。

translations.literal: He at once pardoned the craftsman and exiled him to a distant region.
translations.idiomatic: He at once pardoned the craftsman and exiled him to a distant region.

sentences.zh: 終太子率更令。

translations.literal: He ended as Director of the Heir Apparent's Directorate of Palace Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as director of the heir apparent's directorate of palace supplies.

sentences.zh: 子瓘，為渝州長史，居母喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: His son Guan served as secretary-general of Yuzhou; while in mourning for his mother he died from grief-induced exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan served as secretary-general of Yu; while mourning his mother he died from grief-induced exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 鈞兄子 嗣業

translations.literal: Jun's elder brother's son Siye
translations.idiomatic: Jun's elder brother's son Siye

sentences.zh: 鈞兄子嗣業，少從煬帝后入突厥，貞觀九年歸，以其知虜曲折，詔領突厥眾。

translations.literal: Jun's elder brother's son Siye, in youth followed the empress of Emperor Yang into the Turks; in the ninth year of Zhenguan he returned, and because he knew the barbarians' twists and turns, was ordered to lead the Turkic peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's elder brother's son Siye had followed Empress Xiao of Emperor Yang into the Turks in his youth; he returned in the ninth year of Zhenguan, and because he knew the nomads' ways was ordered to lead the Turkic peoples.

sentences.zh: 擢累鴻臚卿，兼單于都護府長史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently secretary-general of the Chanyu Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to minister of ceremonies and concurrently secretary-general of the Chanyu Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 調露中，突厥叛，嗣業與戰，敗績。

translations.literal: In the Tiaolu era the Turks rebelled; Siye fought them and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiaolu era the Turks rebelled; Siye fought them and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 高宗責曰：「我不殺薛仁貴、郭待封，故使爾至此。

translations.literal: Gaozong reproached him, saying: 'Had I not spared Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng, you would not have come to this.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong reproached him: "Had I not spared Xue Rengui and Guo Daifeng, you would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 然爾門與我家有雅舊，故貸死。

translations.literal: Yet your clan and my house have long-standing cordial ties, so I spare you from death.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet your clan and my house have long-standing ties, so I spare you from death.

sentences.zh: 」乃流桂州。

translations.literal: He was then exiled to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then exiled to Gui.

sentences.zh: 瓘子 嵩

translations.literal: Guan's son Song
translations.idiomatic: Guan's son Song

sentences.zh: 嵩，瓘子，貌偉秀，美須髯。

translations.literal: Song, Guan's son, had a grand and handsome appearance, with fine beard and whiskers.
translations.idiomatic: Song, son of Guan, was imposing and handsome, with a splendid beard.

sentences.zh: 始，娶會稽賀晦女，僚婿陸象先，宰相子，時為洛陽尉，已有名，士爭往交，而嵩汩汩未仕，人不之異。

translations.literal: At the beginning he took as wife the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji; his colleague by marriage Lu Xiangxian was a prime minister's son and at that time was magistrate of Luoyang, already renowned, and gentlemen vied to associate with him—while Song, obscure and yet unsalaried, people did not regard him as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he married the daughter of He Hui of Kuaiji. His colleague by marriage Lu Xiangxian, son of a chief minister and then magistrate of Luoyang, was already famous, and men rushed to befriend him; Song, obscure and still without office, drew no special notice.

sentences.zh: 夏榮者善相，謂象先曰：「君後十年，貴冠人臣，然不若蕭郎位高年艾，舉門蕃熾。

translations.literal: One Xia Rong excelled at physiognomy and said to Xiangxian: "Within ten years you will be noblest among ministers, yet you will not equal Young Master Xiao in lofty rank, great age, and a flourishing household."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Xia Rong was skilled in physiognomy. He told Xiangxian, "In ten years you will stand at the head of the ministers, but you will not match the Xiao gentleman for rank, longevity, and a house in full flower."

sentences.zh: 」時人不許。

translations.literal: At that time people did not credit it.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time did not believe him.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以兵部尚書領朔方節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as Minister of War he was appointed to head the Shuofang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (726) he was made Minister of War and concurrent military commissioner of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 既赴軍，有詔供帳餞定鼎門外，玄宗賦詩勞行。

translations.literal: When he had gone to the army, an edict ordered provisions and a farewell feast outside the Dingding Gate, and Emperor Xuanzong composed a poem to comfort him on his departure.
translations.idiomatic: After he took up his command, the court ordered supplies and a send-off feast outside the Dingding Gate, and Xuanzong wrote a poem to honor his departure.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃大將悉諸邏恭祿及燭龍莽布支陷瓜州，執刺史田元獻；

translations.literal: It happened that the Tibetan grand generals Sinolucigonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi seized Guazhou and seized the prefect Tian Yuanxian;
translations.idiomatic: About then the Tibetan generals Sinolucigonglu and Zhulong Mangbuzhi captured Guazhou and took the prefect Tian Yuanxian prisoner;

sentences.zh: 回紇又殺涼州守將王君㚟，河、隴大震。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs also killed Wang Junzuo, defending general of Liangzhou, and the Yellow River and Longxi regions were greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs also killed Wang Junzuo, the garrison commander of Liangzhou, throwing the He and Long regions into alarm.

sentences.zh: 帝擇堪任邊者，徙嵩河西節度使，判涼州事，封蘭陵縣子。

translations.literal: The emperor chose one fit to serve on the border and transferred Song to be military commissioner of Hexi, with concurrent authority over Liangzhou, enfeoffing him as Viscount of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor chose someone capable on the frontier, moved Song to military commissioner of Hexi with concurrent charge of Liangzhou, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 嵩表裴寬、郭虛己、牛仙客置幕府，以建康軍使張守珪為瓜州刺史，完樹陴塢，懷保邊人。

translations.literal: Song memorialized to have Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke placed in his secretariat; he appointed the Jian'ang army commissioner Zhang Shougui as prefect of Guazhou, completed ramparts and forts, and cherished and protected the border people.
translations.idiomatic: Song recommended Pei Kuan, Guo Xuji, and Niu Xianke for his staff, made Zhang Shougui of the Jian'ang army prefect of Guazhou, rebuilt walls and forts, and looked after the frontier population.

sentences.zh: 于時悉諸邏恭祿威詹諸部，吐蕃倚其健噬邊，嵩乃縱反間，示疑端，贊普果誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Sinolucigonglu's prestige extended over the tribes; the Tibetans relied on his strength to ravage the border. Song then spread counter-intelligence and showed signs of suspicion, and the tsenpo indeed executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sinolucigonglu then dominated the tribal confederations, and Tibet used his prowess to harry the frontier. Song sowed discord and planted doubts until the Tibetan king had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 使悉末明攻瓜州，守珪拒甚力，虜引卻。

translations.literal: He sent Ximo Ming to attack Guazhou; Shougui resisted with great force, and the barbarians withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Ximo Ming was sent against Guazhou, Shougui resisted fiercely and drove the enemy back.

sentences.zh: 會鄯州都督張志亮破賊青海西，嵩又遣副將杜賓客率強弩四千與吐蕃戰祁連城下，自晨鬥迄晡，乃大潰，斬一將，虜哭震山谷。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Zhiliang, military governor of Zhengzhou, defeated the enemy west of Qinghai; Song also sent the deputy commander Du Binke leading four thousand crossbowmen to battle the Tibetans below Qilian City—from morning fought until the afternoon watch, then a great rout, beheading one general, and the barbarians' weeping shook the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhiliang, governor of Zheng, routed the enemy west of Qinghai, Song sent his deputy Du Binke with four thousand crossbowmen to fight the Tibetans at Qilian City. From dawn until evening they battled; the Tibetans broke utterly, a general was killed, and their laments echoed through the ravines.

sentences.zh: 露布至，帝大悅，授嵩同中書門下三品，又官一子，恩顧第一。

translations.literal: When the victory report arrived, the emperor was greatly pleased and appointed Song as co-equal in rank with the chiefs of the Secretariat and the Department of State Affairs; he also enfeoffed one son with office, his favor foremost.
translations.idiomatic: When news of victory arrived, the emperor was delighted, made Song a participant in policy at the third rank, granted office to a son, and favored him above all others.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進兼中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he advanced to concurrent chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was further appointed chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自張說罷宰相，令缺四年，嵩得之，然常遙領河西節度。

translations.literal: From the time Zhang Yue left the post of chief minister the office had been vacant four years; Song obtained it, yet he often held the Hexi military commission at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zhang Yue had left office, the chief ministership had stood empty for four years; Song finally held it, but continued to hold the Hexi command remotely.

sentences.zh: 在公慎密，人莫見其際。

translations.literal: In public office he was prudent and secretive; no one could see his inner workings.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was cautious and impenetrable; none could discern his purpose.

sentences.zh: 子衡，尚新昌公主。

translations.literal: His son Heng married Princess Xinchang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heng married Princess Xinchang.

sentences.zh: 嵩妻入謁，帝呼為親家，儀物貴甚。

translations.literal: When Song's wife entered to pay homage, the emperor addressed her as in-law; the ritual objects were exceedingly fine.
translations.idiomatic: When Song's wife came to court, the emperor called her his kin by marriage, and the ceremonial gifts were magnificent.

sentences.zh: 俄封徐國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 初，裴光庭與嵩數不協，光庭卒，帝委嵩擇相，嵩推韓休。

translations.literal: At first Pei Guangting and Song had often been at odds; when Guangting died, the emperor entrusted Song to choose a chief minister, and Song recommended Han Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guangting and Song had long been at odds. When Guangting died, the emperor asked Song to name a successor; Song proposed Han Xiu.

sentences.zh: 及休同位，峭正不相假，至校曲直帝前。

translations.literal: When Xiu shared the post, stern and upright, each gave the other no quarter, even arguing right and wrong before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiu shared power, the two clashed—each unyielding and upright—and even disputed right and wrong before the throne.

sentences.zh: 嵩慚，乞骸骨。

translations.literal: Song was ashamed and requested his bones—that is, retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Song asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 帝慰之曰：「朕未厭卿，何庸去乎？

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "We have not yet tired of you—why should you leave?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him: "I am not yet weary of you—why would you go?"

sentences.zh: 」嵩伏曰：「臣待罪宰相，爵位既極，幸陛下未厭，得以乞身。

translations.literal: Song prostrated himself and said: "Your servant, holding office as chief minister though guilty of faults, has already reached the summit of rank and titles. By fortune Your Majesty has not yet tired of me, so I may beg my person—that is, retirement."
translations.idiomatic: Song prostrated himself and said, "Your servant has served as chief minister and reached the summit of rank. Fortunate that Your Majesty is not yet weary of me, I beg leave to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 有如厭臣，首領且不保，又安得自遂？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty should tire of your servant, even my head could not be preserved—how then could I have my own way?"
translations.idiomatic: If you should tire of me, I could not keep my head—how then could I go my own way?"

sentences.zh: 」因流涕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept.
translations.idiomatic: He wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 帝為改容曰：「卿言切矣，朕未能決。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression changed and he said: "Your words are cutting; we have not yet been able to decide."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed. "Your words cut deep; I cannot decide yet."

sentences.zh: 弟歸，夕當有詔。

translations.literal: Return home, younger brother—this evening there will be an edict."
translations.idiomatic: "Go home, brother—tonight you will receive an edict."

sentences.zh: 」俄遣高力士詔嵩曰：「朕將爾留，而君臣誼當有始有卒者。

translations.literal: Soon he sent Gao Lishi with an edict to Song, saying: "We wished to keep you, yet the propriety between ruler and minister ought to have beginning and end."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gao Lishi came with the emperor's words: "I wished to keep you, but the bond between ruler and minister ought to have a beginning and an end."

sentences.zh: 」乃授尚書右丞相，與休皆罷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Right Chief of the Department of State Affairs, and both he and Xiu were dismissed from the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Song was made Right Chief of the Department of State Affairs, and both he and Xiu left the chief ministry.

sentences.zh: 是日，荊州進黃甘，帝以紫帉包賜之。

translations.literal: That day Jingzhou presented yellow sweet oranges; the emperor wrapped them in purple silk and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: That day Jingzhou sent golden oranges; the emperor wrapped them in purple silk and gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 擢子華給事中。

translations.literal: He promoted his son Hua to memorial drafter in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted his son Hua to Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，進太子太師。

translations.literal: After a long while he advanced to Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 而幽州節度使張守珪坐賂中人牛仙童得罪，李林甫素忌嵩，因言嵩嘗以城南墅遺仙童，貶青州刺史。

translations.literal: But Zhang Shougui, military commissioner of Youzhou, was implicated for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong; Li Linfu had long resented Song and therefore said Song had once given his villa south of the city to Xiantong—Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shougui of Youzhou was punished for bribing the eunuch Niu Xiantong. Li Linfu, who had long envied Song, claimed Song had once given his south-city villa to Xiantong, and Song was demoted to prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋復拜太子太師。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 固請老，見許。

translations.literal: He firmly requested old-age retirement and was granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed for retirement and was allowed to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 嵩退，脩蒔園區，優遊自怡。

translations.literal: Song retired, cultivated and planted his garden estate, and amused himself at ease.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement Song tended his gardens and passed his days in ease.

sentences.zh: 家饒財，而華為工部侍郎，衡以尚主位三品，就養，年逾八十，士豔其榮。

translations.literal: The household was rich in wealth; Hua was Vice Minister of Works, Heng by marrying a princess held third rank—all supported him in his declining years; past eighty years, gentlemen envied his glory.
translations.idiomatic: The family was wealthy; Hua was Vice Minister of Works, Heng of third rank through his imperial marriage—they supported him in his old age past eighty, and scholars marveled at his good fortune.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載卒，贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao he died and was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Tianbao 8 (749) and was posthumously honored as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 嵩子 華

translations.literal: Song's son: Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Song's son Hua

sentences.zh: 華，謹重方雅，有家法，嗣爵。

translations.literal: Hua was prudent, grave, square, and elegant; he upheld the family rules and inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Hua was careful, dignified, and refined; he maintained the family discipline and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era he was Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 祿山亂，陷賊，逼守魏州。

translations.literal: When the An Lushan rebellion broke out, he was trapped among the rebels and compelled to hold Wei Prefecture for them.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose, Hua fell into rebel hands and was forced to hold Wei Prefecture for them.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀攻安慶緒於相州，華間道奉表，欲舉魏以應，為賊所執。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi attacked An Qingxu at Xiang Prefecture; Hua by a hidden route submitted a memorial, intending to raise Wei to answer the loyal side, but was seized by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Ziyi besieged An Qingxu at Xiang, Hua sent a secret memorial offering to surrender Wei to the loyal cause; the rebels seized him.

sentences.zh: 會崔光遠得魏州，破械出之。

translations.literal: It happened that Cui Guangyuan took Wei Prefecture and broke his shackles to release him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guangyuan captured Wei, he broke Hua's chains and freed him.

sentences.zh: 魏人德華庇免，爭來詣光遠乞留，有詔即授刺史。

translations.literal: The people of Wei credited Hua's sheltering and sparing them and vied to go to Guangyuan begging that he be kept; an edict immediately appointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei remembered how Hua had protected them and thronged to Cui Guangyuan begging that he remain; the court at once named him prefect.

sentences.zh: 思明反，子儀懼復失華，乃表崔光遠代之，而召置軍中。

translations.literal: When Si Ming rebelled, Ziyi feared losing Hua again and therefore memorialized to have Cui Guangyuan replace him, while summoning Hua to place him in the army staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming rebelled, Guo Ziyi, fearing to lose Hua again, had Cui Guangyuan replace him and summoned Hua to his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 相州兵潰，華還朝，猶以汙賊降試秘書少監。

translations.literal: When the army at Xiang collapsed, Hua returned to court, yet because he had been stained by surrender to the rebels he was provisionally appointed Junior Mentor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After the rout at Xiang, Hua returned to court but, tainted by his surrender to the rebels, was provisionally made Junior Mentor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 稍遷尚書右丞，擢河中晉、絳節度使。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and promoted to military commissioner of Hedong overseeing Jin and Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, then to military commissioner of Hedong over Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 上元初，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent participation in Council deliberation and regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shangyuan (760) he became Vice Director of the Secretariat and participant in policy deliberation.

sentences.zh: 李輔國用事，求宰相，華拒之，輔國怨。

translations.literal: Li Fuguo held power and sought the chief ministry; Hua refused him and Fuguo bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo, who held real power, sought the chief ministership; Hua refused, and Fuguo resented it.

sentences.zh: 會肅宗大漸，矯詔罷華為禮部尚書，引元載以代。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was gravely ill, a forged edict removed Hua to Minister of Rites and brought in Yuan Zai to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: As Suzong lay dying, a forged edict removed Hua to Minister of Rites and installed Yuan Zai in his place.

sentences.zh: 方代宗諒暗，載助輔國，貶華為峽州司馬，卒。

translations.literal: Just then Emperor Daizong was in mourning seclusion; Zai assisted Fuguo and demoted Hua to militia-commander of Xia Prefecture; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was then in mourning; Yuan Zai aided Fuguo, demoted Hua to militia-commander of Xia, and Hua died.

sentences.zh: 二子：恒、悟。

translations.literal: Two sons: Heng and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Heng and Wu.

sentences.zh: 嵩孫 復

translations.literal: Song's grandson: Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Song's grandson Fu

sentences.zh: 復，字履初，衡子。

translations.literal: Fu, style name Lüchu, was Heng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu, styled Lüchu, was son of Heng.

sentences.zh: 生戚裏，姻從豪汰，以服禦輿馬相誇，復常衣垢弊，居一室，學自力，非名士夙儒不與遊，以清操顯。

translations.literal: Born in the imperial affines, his kin and companions were extravagant and dissolute, boasting in robes and carriage horses; Fu often wore grimy worn clothes, dwelt in one room, studied by his own effort, associated only with renowned gentlemen and veteran scholars, and was distinguished for pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Though born among the imperial kin, whose relatives paraded in fine dress and carriages, Fu wore shabby clothes, lived in a single room, studied alone, kept company only with men of learning and principle, and became known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 華每歎曰：「此子當興吾宗！

translations.literal: Hua often sighed and said: "This son will surely raise our clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Hua would often sigh, "This boy will revive our house!"

sentences.zh: 」推主廕為宮門郎。

translations.literal: He recommended and secured for him the inherited yin privilege as gate officer of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He secured for him the yin privilege appointment as palace gate officer.

sentences.zh: 廣德中，歲大饑，家百口，不自振，議鬻昭應墅。

translations.literal: In the Guangde era there was great famine; the household numbered a hundred mouths and could not support itself; they discussed selling the villa at Zhaoying.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangde (763–764), when famine struck, the household of a hundred mouths could not sustain itself and debated selling the Zhaoying villa.

sentences.zh: 宰相王縉欲得之，使弟紘說曰：「以君才宜在左右，胡不以墅奉丞相取右職？

translations.literal: The chief minister Wang Jin wished to obtain it and sent his younger brother Hong to persuade him, saying: "With your talent you ought to be at the ruler's side—why not present the villa to the chief minister to obtain a post at the right hand?"
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Wang Jin wanted the estate and sent his brother Hong to say, "A man of your ability belongs at the emperor's side. Why not give the villa to the chief minister and win a post at court?"

sentences.zh: 」復曰：「鬻先人墅以濟孀單，吾何用美官，使門內餒且寒乎？

translations.literal: Fu said: "To sell our ancestors' villa to relieve widows and the destitute—why should I want a fine office and let our gate be hungry and cold within?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied, "I would sell my ancestors' estate to feed widows and orphans—why should I take a glittering title and leave my household hungry and cold?"

sentences.zh: 」縉憾之，由是廢。

translations.literal: Jin resented this and thereafter had him dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin resented the refusal and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 數歲，乃曆歙、池二州刺史，治狀應條。

translations.literal: Several years later he served in turn as prefect of She and Chi; his governance records met every criterion.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he governed She and Chi in succession, his records meeting every standard.

sentences.zh: 遷湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be observation commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 改同州刺史，歲歉，州有京畿觀察使儲粟，復輒發以貸人，有司劾治，詔削階，停刺史。

translations.literal: He was changed to prefect of Tong; the year was poor; the prefecture had grain stored by the metropolitan observation commissioner—Fu promptly opened it to lend to the people; the authorities impeached him, and an edict reduced his rank and suspended him as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Tong in a lean year, he opened grain stored for the capital region and lent it to the people. The authorities prosecuted him; he was reduced in rank and relieved of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或吊之，復曰：「苟利於人，胡責之辭！

translations.literal: When someone condoled with him, Fu said: "If it benefits the people, why trouble over words of reproach?"
translations.idiomatic: When someone condoled with him, Fu said, "If it helped the people, what matter the reproach?"

sentences.zh: 」久乃拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 普王為襄漢元帥，進復戶部尚書、統軍長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Pu was grand marshal of Xiang and Han, Fu was advanced to Minister of Revenue and Chief of Staff for the unified army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Pu was made grand marshal of Xiang-Han, Fu was promoted to Minister of Revenue and chief of staff for the unified command.

sentences.zh: 舊制謂「行軍長史」，德宗以復父諱更之。

translations.literal: The old regulation called the post "campaign chief of staff"; Emperor Dezong, because of Fu's father's taboo name, changed the title.
translations.idiomatic: The old title had been "campaign chief of staff"; Dezong changed it to avoid Fu's father's name (Heng).

sentences.zh: 未行，扈狩奉天。

translations.literal: Before he set out, he accompanied the hunt at Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, the court fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 帝惡庳隘，欲西如鳳翔依張鎰。

translations.literal: The emperor disliked the low and narrow place and wished to go west to Fengxiang to rely on Zhang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found Fengtian cramped and wished to move west to Fengxiang and Zhang Yi.

sentences.zh: 復曰：「鳳翔乃泚舊兵，今泚悖亂，當有同惡者。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Fengxiang was Zhu Ci's old troops; now Zhu Ci rebels against order—there should be those of like wicked intent."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Fengxiang was Zhu Ci's old command. Now that Zhu Ci has rebelled, there will be men who share his cause."

sentences.zh: 雖鎰，臣畏不免。

translations.literal: Even Zhang Yi—your servant fears we would not escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even with Zhang Yi, I fear we would not be safe.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕業行，留一日以驗爾言！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "We are already on the road—stay one day to verify your words!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "We are already on the march—stay one day and we shall see if you are right."

sentences.zh: 」俄而鎰為李楚琳所害，於是拜吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon Zhang Yi was killed by Li Chulin; thereupon Fu was appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent participation in Council deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Within a day Zhang Yi was murdered by Li Chulin, and Fu was made Minister of Personnel and participant in policy deliberation.

sentences.zh: 復嘗言：「艱難以來，始用宦者監軍，權望太重，是曹正可委宮掖事，兵要政機，叵使參領。

translations.literal: Fu once said: "Since our times of hardship, eunuchs have begun to supervise armies; their authority and prestige are too heavy. That lot may rightly be entrusted with palace and inner service matters—military essentials and government mechanisms ought not be permitted to them to share in leading."
translations.idiomatic: Fu once said, "Since the troubles began, eunuchs have supervised armies and grown too powerful. They should manage palace affairs alone; they must not touch military and governmental power."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下厥初清明，自楊炎、盧杞妨命穢盛德，播越及茲。

translations.literal: Again he said: "Your Majesty at first was clear and bright; from Yang Yan and Lu Qi obstructing commands and defiling great virtue, exile and wandering extend to this day."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Your Majesty began his reign enlightened, but Yang Yan and Lu Qi obstructed your orders and stained your virtue until exile brought us here."

sentences.zh: 今阽于危，當懲乂前敗。

translations.literal: Now on the brink of peril, you ought to take warning from and rectify former failures.
translations.idiomatic: Now at the brink of ruin, you must learn from past failures.

sentences.zh: 」因述君臣大端，即自言：「若使臣依阿偷免，不敢當宰相。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set forth the great principles between ruler and minister, then said of himself: "If you would have your servant fawn and connive to escape blame, I dare not hold the post of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the bond between ruler and minister, then said, "If you wish me to fawn and scheme for safety, I cannot serve as chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」杞對上或諂諛阿匼，復厲言：「杞詞不正！

translations.literal: When Qi spoke to the emperor he would sometimes flatter and fawn; Fu spoke sternly: "Qi's words are not upright!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qi flattered the emperor, Fu said sharply, "Qi's words are crooked!"

sentences.zh: 」帝色眙，謂左右曰：「復慢我。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression was startled and he said to those at hand: "Fu is slighting me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed. He told his attendants, "Fu is treating me with disrespect."

sentences.zh: 」因詔復充山南、江淮、湖南、嶺南等道宣撫、安慰使。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict appointed Fu commissioner to proclaim and reassure for the circuits of Shannan, Jiang-Huai, Hunan, Lingnan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore sent out as commissioner to proclaim and comfort the circuits of Shannan, Jiang-Huai, Hunan, Lingnan, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 興元初，進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xingyuan (784) he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 初，淮南陳少游左附李希烈，而張鎰判官韋皋殺邠、隴叛卒，不應楚琳。

translations.literal: At first Chen Shaoyou of Huainan leaned in support of Li Xilie, while Zhang Yi's aide Wei Gao killed the mutinous troops of Bin and Long and did not respond to Chu Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan had sided with Li Xilie, while Wei Gao, aide to Zhang Yi, executed the Bin-Long mutineers and refused to follow Li Chulin.

sentences.zh: 復還執政，建言：「陛下反正，功臣已貴矣，唯甄善汰惡為未明。

translations.literal: When Fu returned to hold power, he offered counsel: "Your Majesty has returned to the right path; meritorious servants are already honored—only sorting the good and culling the wicked is not yet clear."
translations.idiomatic: Back in power, Fu said, "Your Majesty has restored order and rewarded the loyal, but you have not yet distinguished the worthy from the wicked.

sentences.zh: 少遊位將相，首臣賊，皋名淺官下，獨挺挺抗忠。

translations.literal: Shaoyou holds the rank of general and chief minister, yet was foremost in serving the rebel; Gao's name is shallow and his office low, yet alone he stands tall in loyal resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyou holds high rank yet led the way in serving the rebel; Gao is obscure in rank yet stood alone in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 如以皋代少遊，則天下嘹然知逆順之理。

translations.literal: If Gao were used to replace Shaoyou, then the empire would ringingly know the principle of rebellion and submission."
translations.idiomatic: If Gao replaced Shaoyou, all the realm would clearly see the difference between loyal and traitor."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 復出，中官馬欽緒揖宰相劉從一，附耳語，既而從一密諗復曰：「有詔與公議向所奏，不欲李勉、盧翰聞知。

translations.literal: When Fu went out, the eunuch Ma Qinxu bowed to the chief minister Liu Congyi and spoke in his ear; presently Congyi secretly informed Fu: "There is an edict to discuss with you what was just memorialized; we do not wish Li Mian and Lu Han to hear of it."
translations.idiomatic: As Fu left, the eunuch Ma Qinxu bowed to Chief Minister Liu Congyi and whispered. Congyi then told Fu privately, "The emperor wishes to discuss your proposal with you alone; Li Mian and Lu Han are not to know."

sentences.zh: 」復曰：「堯、舜有'僉曰'之言，朝廷大事尚當謀及公卿。

translations.literal: Fu said: "Yao and Shun had the saying 'the multitude said'; great affairs of court ought still to be deliberated with the chief ministers and grandees."
translations.idiomatic: Fu replied, "Even Yao and Shun said 'the multitude proposes.' Great matters of state should be discussed with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 如勉等非其人，當罷去。

translations.literal: If Mian and the rest are not the right men, they ought to be dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: If Li Mian and the others are unfit, dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 既曰宰相，而謀議可獨避之乎？

translations.literal: Since they are called chief ministers, how can counsel and deliberation be deliberately kept from them alone?"
translations.idiomatic: But if they are chief ministers, how can state business be kept from them?"

sentences.zh: 今與公行此或可，第恐浸以生常，政由是敝。

translations.literal: To go along with you on this now might perhaps be possible, but I fear it will gradually become routine and government will thereby decay."
translations.idiomatic: I might yield to you this once, but I fear it will become habit—and government will suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 」從一以聞，帝不悅。

translations.literal: Congyi reported this; the emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Congyi reported Fu's words; the emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 復辭疾上政事，許之。

translations.literal: Fu pleaded illness and submitted his governmental affairs; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Fu pleaded illness and resigned from office; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 弟升，尚郜國大長公主，肅宗女也。

translations.literal: His younger brother Sheng married the Grand Eldest Princess of Gao, daughter of Emperor Suzong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Sheng had married the Grand Eldest Princess of Gao, a daughter of Suzong.

sentences.zh: 升早卒，主以奸蠱事再得罪廢，諸子悉逐醜地，女為皇太子妃，太子請離婚，帝銜曩忮，故復坐是檢校太子左庶子，廢居饒州。

translations.literal: Sheng died early; the princess, because of sorcery and poisoning affairs, twice offended and was deposed; all her sons were banished to vile regions; her daughter was consort to the crown prince, and the prince requested divorce. The emperor harbored old resentment, and therefore Fu by this connection was made acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent while deposed and dwelling in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng died young. The princess was twice disgraced and deposed over witchcraft; her sons were sent to remote exile; her daughter married the crown prince, who sought divorce. The emperor still nursed old grievances, and Fu was demoted to acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and exiled to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 788, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 復望閥高華，厲名節，不通狎流俗。

translations.literal: Fu looked to illustrious clans and lofty lineage, upheld reputation and integrity, and did not associate with frivolous common customs.
translations.idiomatic: Fu aspired to the prestige of great houses, held fast to honor, and kept his distance from the coarse world.

sentences.zh: 及為相，臨事嚴方，數咈帝意，故居位亟解。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister, in handling affairs he was strict and upright, repeatedly going against the emperor's intent, and therefore his tenure in office was repeatedly cut short.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he was stern and principled, often crossing the emperor, and was dismissed from office again and again.

sentences.zh: 然性孝友，既貶晏然，口未嘗言所累。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was filial and friendly; once demoted he was serene, and his mouth never spoke of what had harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was devoted to family and friends; after demotion he remained calm and never complained of what had brought him down.

sentences.zh: 復子湛。

translations.literal: Fu's son was Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛子寘，咸通中位宰相，無顯功，史逸其傳。

translations.literal: Zhan's son Zhen, during Xiantong held the post of chief minister, with no notable achievements; the histories omit his biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's son Zhen became chief minister in the Xiantong era but accomplished nothing of note, and the histories pass over him without a full biography.

sentences.zh: 華孫 俛

translations.literal: Hua's grandson Mian
translations.idiomatic: Hua's grandson Mian

sentences.zh: 俛，字思謙，恒子。

translations.literal: Mian, style name Siqian, was Heng's son.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, styled Siqian, was the son of Heng.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，及進士第，又以賢良方正對策異等，拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: During Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi examination, and again, in the examination for Worthy and Upright candidates, his policy answers were graded exceptional; he was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyuan era he took the jinshi degree and, in a special examination for men of talent, ranked at the top; he was made Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，召為翰林學士，凡三年，進知制誥。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanhe he was summoned as Hanlin Academician; after three years in all he advanced to Drafting Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In 811 he entered the Hanlin Academy; three years later he was promoted to draft edicts for the throne.

sentences.zh: 會張仲方以李吉甫數調發疲天下，訾其諡，憲宗怒，逐仲方，而俛坐與善，奪學士，下除太僕少卿。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhang Zhongfang, because Li Jifu had repeatedly requisitioned and mobilized troops until the empire was exhausted, criticized his posthumous title; Emperor Xianzong was angry and expelled Zhongfang, while Mian was implicated for being on good terms with him, stripped of his academicianship, and demoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhongfang attacked Li Jifu's posthumous name—arguing that his repeated levies had worn the realm out—Xianzong banished Zhongfang and punished Mian for their friendship by removing him from the Hanlin and demoting him to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛薦為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo recommended him as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo had him appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鎛與令狐楚皆善俛，兩人同輔政，數稱其善，故帝待俛厚。

translations.literal: Bo and Linghu Chu were both on good terms with Mian; the two together assisted in government and repeatedly praised his merits, and therefore the emperor treated Mian generously.
translations.idiomatic: Bo and Linghu Chu both favored Mian; as co-regents they praised him often, and the emperor treated him with marked regard.

sentences.zh: 襲徐國公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，逐鎛，議所以代者，楚薦之，授中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: When Muzong ascended, Bo was expelled; as they deliberated who should replace him, Chu recommended Mian, who was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery, then advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After Muzong came to the throne and dismissed Bo, Chu recommended Mian as his replacement; Mian was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister, then promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃寇涇州，調兵護邊，帝因問：「兵法有必勝乎？

translations.literal: The Tibetans raided Jing Prefecture; troops were mobilized to guard the border. The emperor thereupon asked: "In the art of war, is there certain victory?"
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans attacked Jingzhou, troops were sent to the frontier, and the emperor asked, "Is there such a thing as a sure win in war?"

sentences.zh: 」俛曰：「兵兇器，聖人不得已用之，故武不可玩，玩則無震。

translations.literal: Mian said: "Arms are an inauspicious instrument; the sage uses them only when he has no choice. Therefore martial power must not be trifled with—if trifled with, there is no awe."
translations.idiomatic: Mian replied, "Weapons are instruments of violence; a sage employs them only when he must. War must never be treated lightly—treat it lightly and its deterrent fails."

sentences.zh: 夫以仁討不仁，以義討不義，先招懷，後掩襲，故有不殺厲，不禽二毛，不犯田稼，其救人如免水火，此必勝術也。

translations.literal: To use benevolence to chastise the unbenevolent, righteousness to chastise the unrighteous—first win men by conciliation, then strike by surprise. Hence there is not killing the sick, not capturing the gray-haired, not trampling the crops; to rescue people as from fire and flood—this is the art of certain victory.
translations.idiomatic: Use benevolence against cruelty and justice against injustice: win hearts first, strike only afterward. Do not kill the wounded, take the aged prisoner, or trample the fields; rescue the people as you would pull them from flood or flame—that is how victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 若乃以小不忍輕任干戈，師曲而敵怨，非徒不勝，又將自危，是以聖王慎於兵。

translations.literal: If one lightly takes up arms over petty impatience, the army is unjust and the enemy resentful—not only will one fail to win, but one will also endanger oneself. Therefore the sage king is cautious with arms.
translations.idiomatic: But if petty irritation leads you lightly to war, your cause is crooked and your foes enraged—you will not only lose but put yourself in peril. That is why sage rulers handle arms with the utmost care.

sentences.zh: 」帝重其言。

translations.literal: The emperor valued his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his counsel seriously.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔俛撰王承宗先銘，俛奏：「承宗比不臣，迷而後復，臣不忍稱道其先。

translations.literal: Once the emperor ordered Mian to compose the funerary inscription for Wang Chengzong's forebear. Mian memorialized: "Chengzong was formerly disloyal, went astray and only later returned; your servant cannot bear to praise his ancestor."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once ordered Mian to write an epitaph for Wang Chengzong's father. Mian replied, "Chengzong was once a rebel who strayed and only later submitted; I cannot in good conscience praise his forebears."

sentences.zh: 又辭成當有餉謝，拒之，則非朝廷撫納意；

translations.literal: Moreover, when the text is finished there ought to be a gift of thanks; to refuse it would not accord with the court's intent to comfort and accept;
translations.idiomatic: And when the text is done, custom calls for a gift of thanks—to refuse it would slight the court's policy of reconciliation;

sentences.zh: 受之，臣誼不當取。

translations.literal: to accept it would be improper for your servant's principles to take.
translations.idiomatic: yet to accept it would violate what a minister ought to do."

sentences.zh: 」帝善而止。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚罷執政，西川節度使王播賂權幸求宰相，俛劾播纖佞不可汙台宰，帝不許。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu was removed from holding power; Wang Bo, military governor of Xichuan, bribed the powerful favorites to seek the chief ministership. Mian impeached Bo as a fawning sycophant unfit to stain the post of chief of the terrace and altar; the emperor did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: After Linghu Chu left office, Wang Bo of Xichuan bribed court favorites to win the chancellorship. Mian impeached him as a sycophant unfit for the highest office; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 自請罷，冀有感寤，帝亦不省。

translations.literal: He requested his own dismissal, hoping the emperor would be moved to understanding; the emperor also did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Mian asked to resign, hoping the emperor would take the hint; he did not.

sentences.zh: 俄罷為尚書左僕射，用播為鹽鐵使，後卒相，俛自謂輔政淺，固辭僕射，換吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was removed and made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Bo was used as Salt and Iron Commissioner and in the end became chief minister. Mian considered his own tenure in assisting government shallow, firmly declined the vice directorship, and was exchanged to Minister of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Mian was demoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while Bo was made Salt and Iron Commissioner and eventually chief minister. Mian, judging his own service insubstantial, refused the vice directorship and took the post of Minister of Civil Office instead.

sentences.zh: 又避選事，徙兵部，移病求分司，不許。

translations.literal: Again he avoided selection affairs, was transferred to the Ministry of War, pleaded illness and sought a nominal post in the Eastern or Western Capital, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He then shunned personnel matters, was moved to the Ministry of War, and pleaded illness for a sinecure in Luoyang; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 授太子少保，為同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and made Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 復以少保分司東都。

translations.literal: Again, as Junior Mentor he held nominal office in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in Luoyang in the same nominal capacity.

sentences.zh: 母韋，賢明，治家嚴，俛雖宰相，侍左右如褐衣時。

translations.literal: His mother, née Wei, was worthy and wise; in governing the household she was strict. Though Mian was chief minister, in attending at her side he was as in the days of coarse cloth.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, of the Wei clan, was intelligent and ran the household with strict discipline; even as chief minister, Mian waited on her as humbly as when he wore commoner's garb.

sentences.zh: 居喪哀毀。

translations.literal: In mourning he was grief-stricken to the point of wasting away.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he grieved so deeply that he nearly ruined his health.

sentences.zh: 既老，家於洛，歲時賓客請謝，以為煩，乃舍濟源墅，自放山野，優遊窮年。

translations.literal: Once old, he made his home in Luoyang; at the seasons guests would come to pay respects and take leave, which he found troublesome, and therefore he abandoned his villa at Jiyuan and let himself go in mountains and wilds, roaming at ease year after year.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he settled in Luoyang but found seasonal calls from guests a burden; he gave up his estate at Jiyuan and spent his remaining years wandering freely in the hills.

sentences.zh: 然其居位頗介謹持法，重名器，狹於用人，每除吏，常憂不稱，鮮有簡拔。

translations.literal: Yet in holding office he was rather upright, cautious, and law-abiding; he valued titles and regalia, was narrow in employing men—each time he appointed an official he constantly worried they would not fit the post, and rarely made bold selections.
translations.idiomatic: In office, however, he was rigid, cautious, and legalistic; he prized rank and ceremony and was timid about appointments, always fearing a poor fit and seldom promoting anyone of real merit.

sentences.zh: 穆宗初，兩河底定，俛與段文昌當國，謂四方無虞，遂議大平事，以為武不可黷，勸帝偃革尚文，乃密詔天下鎮兵，十之，歲限一為逃、死，不補，謂之銷兵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Muzong's reign the two He regions were settled; Mian and Duan Wenchang held the state, deeming the four quarters free of worry, and therefore deliberated on great peace—holding that martial power must not be profaned, they urged the emperor to lay down arms and exalt culture. Thereupon a secret edict to the empire's garrison troops: of every ten, yearly limit one as desertion or death without replacement—this was called troop reduction.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Muzong's reign, with the Hebei provinces pacified, Mian and Duan Wenchang assumed that the realm was secure and set about planning for lasting peace. Arguing that war must not be abused, they urged the emperor to disarm and promote culture. A secret order went out to garrisons nationwide: each year, one man in ten was to be struck from the rolls as deserter or dead, with no replacements—a policy called "troop reduction."

sentences.zh: 既而籍卒逋亡，無生業，曹聚山林間為盜賊。

translations.literal: Before long, registered soldiers who had fled and vanished had no livelihood and gathered in bands in mountains and forests to become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon discharged soldiers, with no livelihood, banded together in the hills as outlaws.

sentences.zh: 會硃克融、王廷湊亂燕、趙，一日悉收用之。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou raised turmoil in Yan and Zhao; in a single day they all enlisted and used them.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Kerong and Wang Tingcou rebelled in Yan and Zhao, they recruited these men wholesale in a single day.

sentences.zh: 朝廷調兵不克，乃召募市人烏合，戰輒北，遂復失河朔矣。

translations.literal: The court mobilized troops but could not overcome them; thereupon it recruited townsmen in a rabble host—when they fought they always fled north, and thus the Hebei region was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces failed to suppress them; the court then raised rabbles of townsfolk who were routed at every engagement, and the Hebei provinces were lost anew.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：俛議銷兵，寧不野哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: Mian's proposal of troop reduction—was it not indeed reckless!
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Mian's policy of troop reduction—how naive was that!

sentences.zh: 當此時，河朔雖挈地還天子，而悍卒頑夫開口仰食者故在，彼皆不能自返於本業者也。

translations.literal: At this time, though the Hebei region had brought its territory back to the Son of Heaven, fierce soldiers and stubborn fellows who opened their mouths to be fed by others were still there—they all could not return themselves to their original occupations.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Hebei provinces had submitted their territory to the throne, yet hardened veterans who lived by the sword and knew no other trade remained—they could not simply return to civilian life.

sentences.zh: 又硃克融等客長安，餓且死，不得一官，而俛未有以措置，便欲去兵，使群臣失職，一日叫呼，其從如市，幽、魏相挺，復為賊淵，可謂見豪末而不察輿薪矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhu Kerong and others were guests in Chang'an, starving and near death, yet could not obtain a single office, while Mian had no means to arrange for them and wished at once to remove troops, causing the ministers to lose their posts. In a single day they cried out and their followers were like a market; You and Wei supported one another and again became a lair of bandits. One may say he saw the tip of a hair but did not observe a cartload of firewood.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhu Kerong and his ilk lingered in Chang'an, starving without appointment, and Mian had done nothing for them—yet he would strip away the army and leave such men idle. One day's clamor drew followers like a marketplace; You and Wei rose together and the region became a rebel stronghold again. He saw a hair's breadth but missed the cartload of firewood at his door.

sentences.zh: 宰相非其人，禍可既乎！

translations.literal: When the chief minister is not the right man, can calamity be exhausted?
translations.idiomatic: With the wrong man as chief minister, could disaster end there?

sentences.zh: 華孫 倣

translations.literal: Hua's grandson Fang
translations.idiomatic: Hua's grandson Fang

sentences.zh: 仿，字思道，悟子。

translations.literal: Fang, style name Sidao, was Wu's son.
translations.idiomatic: Fang, styled Sidao, was the son of Wu.

sentences.zh: 大和中，擢進士第。

translations.literal: During Dahe he was selected in the jinshi degree.
