translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 除累給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 宣宗力治，喜直言，嘗以李璲為嶺南節度使，使者已賜節，而仿封還詔書。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong vigorously governed and delighted in straight speech. Once Li Jun was appointed military governor of Lingnan; the envoy had already been given the credential tally, but Fang sealed and returned the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong ruled energetically and welcomed frank counsel. When Li Jun was named governor of Lingnan and the envoy had already been given his commission, Fang sealed the edict and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 帝方作樂，不暇命使，遣優工趨出追之，未及璲所而還。

translations.literal: The emperor was just then making music and had no leisure to order the envoy; he sent a comic performer to hurry out and overtake him, but before reaching Jun's place he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at his diversions and could not summon the envoy himself; he sent a court entertainer racing after him, but the man turned back before he reached Jun.

sentences.zh: 後以封敕脫誤，法當罰，侍講學士孔溫裕曰：「給事中駁奏，為朝廷論得失，與有司奏事不類，不應罰。

translations.literal: Later, because the sealed edict had omissions and errors, by law he ought to be punished. Academician-Expositor Kong Wenyü said: "The Supervising Censor's rebuttal memorials speak for the court on gain and loss; they are not of the same kind as routine submissions by offices, and he ought not to be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Later Fang was liable to punishment because the returned edict was damaged. Kong Wenyü, a lecturer at court, argued, "A Supervising Censor's objections weigh right and wrong for the state—they are not ordinary bureaucratic papers and should not be penalized."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 令狐綯用李琢經略安南，琢以暴遝免，俄起為壽州團練使，仿劾奏琢無所回，時推其直。

translations.literal: Linghu Tao employed Li Zhuo to oversee Annan; Zhuo was removed for violence and indolence, but soon was raised again as regimental commander of Shou Prefecture. Fang impeached and memorialized against Zhuo without yielding, and at the time he was praised for his uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Tao had Li Zhuo pacify Annan; Zhuo was dismissed for brutality and sloth but soon resurfaced as commander at Shouzhou. Fang impeached him without flinching, and contemporaries admired his integrity.

sentences.zh: 自集賢學士拜嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: From Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies he was appointed military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He went from Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies to military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 南方珍賄叢夥，不以入門。

translations.literal: In the south rare gifts and bribes clustered thickly; he did not let them enter his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The south overflowed with rare gifts and bribes, but none crossed his threshold.

sentences.zh: 家人病，取槁梅於廚以和劑，仿知，趣市還之。

translations.literal: When a family member was ill, dried plum was taken from the kitchen to mix medicine; Fang learned of it and hurried to the market to buy and return it.
translations.idiomatic: When a relative fell ill, someone took dried plum from the kitchen stores to compound medicine; Fang learned of it and rushed to market to pay for what had been taken.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，為左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiantong era he became Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 懿宗怠政事，喜佛道，引桑門入禁中為禱祠事，數幸佛廬，廣施予。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong was slack in government affairs, delighted in Buddhism and the Way, brought monks into the forbidden precincts for prayer and sacrifice, repeatedly visited Buddhist halls, and gave broadly in charity.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong neglected government, favored Buddhism and Daoism, brought monks into the palace for rites, often visited temples, and lavished alms.

sentences.zh: 仿諫，以為：「天竺法割愛取滅，非帝王所尚慕。

translations.literal: Fang remonstrated, holding: "The law of India cuts off affection and seeks extinction; it is not what emperors and kings admire and emulate."
translations.idiomatic: Fang remonstrated: "The Indian teaching urges renunciation and extinction of the self—hardly what a monarch should emulate."

sentences.zh: 今筆梵言，口佛音，不若懲謬賞濫罰，振殃祈福。

translations.literal: Now to write Sanskrit words and mouth Buddhist sounds is not as good as punishing error, rewarding the meritorious, curbing reckless bestowal and careless punishment, and rousing fortune to ward off calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Writing Sanskrit and chanting sutras are no substitute for correcting abuses, rewarding merit, restraining reckless grants and punishments, and thereby turning misfortune to blessing.

sentences.zh: 況佛者可以悟取，不可以相求。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Buddha can be attained through awakening; he cannot be sought through appearances.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, enlightenment comes through understanding, not through outward display.

sentences.zh: 」帝雖昏縱，猶嘉歎其言。

translations.literal: Though the emperor was muddled and self-indulgent, he still praised and sighed over his words.
translations.idiomatic: Though muddled and self-indulgent, the emperor still praised his counsel.

sentences.zh: 後官數遷，拜義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: Later his office was repeatedly transferred; he was appointed military governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted through several posts and made military governor of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 滑州瀕河，累歲水壞西北防，仿徙其流遠去，樹堤自固，人得以安。

translations.literal: Hua Prefecture bordered the river; year after year floods ruined the northwestern defenses. Fang diverted the current far away, planted dikes to secure it himself, and the people were able to live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: At Huazhou, on the Yellow River, floods had for years breached the northwestern levees; Fang redirected the channel, built new dikes, and the people lived in safety.

sentences.zh: 以兵部尚書再判度支，進中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: As Minister of War he again concurrently judged the Treasury; he advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister of War he again oversaw the treasury, then became Vice Director of the Secretariat and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 再遷司空、蘭陵縣侯。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Grand Preceptor and Marquis of Lanling County.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Preceptor and Marquis of Lanling.

sentences.zh: 時天下盜起，宦人持兵柄，仿以鯁正為權近所忌。

translations.literal: At the time bandits rose throughout the empire; eunuchs held military power. Fang, for his upright firmness, was resented by those in power close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits roamed the realm and eunuchs held the armies; Fang's stubborn integrity made him hated by the powerful at court.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 倣子 廩

translations.literal: Fang's son Lin
translations.idiomatic: Fang's son Lin

sentences.zh: 子廩，字富侯。

translations.literal: His son Lin, style name Fuhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lin, styled Fuhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He placed in the jinshi examination and was transferred to a Secretariat official.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and was appointed a Secretariat official.

sentences.zh: 仿領南海，解官往侍。

translations.literal: When Fang took charge of the Southern Sea, he resigned office to go and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang took the post in the far south, Lin resigned his own office to accompany and care for him.

sentences.zh: 為人退約少合。

translations.literal: As a man he was retiring and restrained, seldom in accord with others.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was modest and reserved, and made few close friends.

sentences.zh: 南海多穀紙，仿敕諸子繕補殘書。

translations.literal: The Southern Sea had much grain-straw paper; Fang ordered his sons to mend and repair damaged books.
translations.idiomatic: Paper was plentiful in the south, and Fang had his sons repair damaged books from his library.

sentences.zh: 廩諫曰：「州距京師且萬里，書成不可露齎，必貯以囊笥，貪者伺望，得無薏苡嫌乎？

translations.literal: Lin remonstrated: "The prefecture is nearly ten thousand li from the capital; when books are finished they cannot be carried openly—they must be stored in bags and cases, and the greedy will watch and wait. Will there not be the suspicion of the Job's-tears incident?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin objected: "This post is ten thousand li from the capital. Finished books cannot be carried openly—they must be packed in chests, and the greedy will take notice. Will you not invite the suspicion Ma Yuan suffered over his Job's-tears?"

sentences.zh: 」仿曰：「善，吾思不及此。

translations.literal: Fang said: "Good—I did not think as far as this."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "You are right; I had not thought of that."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 廣明初，以諫議大夫知制誥，請厲止夜行以備賊諜，出太倉粟賤估以濟貧民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangming, as Remonstrating Grandee he drafted edicts; he requested stern prohibition of night travel to guard against rebel spies, and release of Great Granary grain at low valuation to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangming era, as Remonstrating Grandee and edict drafter, he urged a strict curfew against rebel spies and the sale of imperial grain at low prices to aid the poor.

sentences.zh: 俄遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made metropolitan governor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 田令孜養子有罪亡，擊捕吏，系獄，請救踵門，廩不納，杖殺之，內外畏讋。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi's adopted son committed a crime and fled; he struck the arresting officer and was imprisoned. Pleas for rescue came in succession at the gate; Lin would not accept them and had him beaten to death. Within and without, all feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: An adopted son of Tian Lingzi committed a crime and fled; he assaulted the arresting officer and was jailed. Supplicants thronged Lin's gate, but he refused them and had the man flogged to death; court and capital alike stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 令孜拒黃巢，以廩為糧料使，辭疾，貶賀州司戶參軍事。

translations.literal: Lingzi resisted Huang Chao and appointed Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to Registrar of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingzi resisted Huang Chao he named Lin grain commissioner; Lin pleaded illness and was demoted to registrar at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 會襄王竊據，挈族逃河朔，鎮冀節度使王鎔厚禮之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiang seized territory by force, he took his clan and fled to the Hebei region; Wang Rong, military governor of Zhenji, treated him with generous courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Xiang seized power, Lin fled north with his family; Wang Rong, governor of Zhenji, received him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 光化中，以給事中召，不至，卒。

translations.literal: During Guanghua he was summoned as Supervising Censor but did not arrive; he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanghua era he was recalled as Supervising Censor but did not come; he died.

sentences.zh: 復曾孫 遘

translations.literal: Fu's great-grandson Gou
translations.idiomatic: Fu's great-grandson Gou

sentences.zh: 遘，字得聖，寘子。

translations.literal: Gou, style name Desheng, was Zhen's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gou, styled Desheng, was the son of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，擢進士第，辟節度府。

translations.literal: During Xiantong he was selected in the jinshi degree and was recruited to a military governor's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era he passed the jinshi and entered a governor's staff.

sentences.zh: 入朝，拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court and was made Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 與韋保衡聯第，而遘姿宇秀偉，氣孤峻，嘗慕李德裕為人。

translations.literal: He and Wei Baoheng graduated in the same year, but Gou's bearing and stature were handsome and grand, his spirit solitary and stern; he once admired Li Deyu's character.
translations.idiomatic: He graduated alongside Wei Baoheng, but Gou was tall and striking, aloof and severe, and had long admired Li Deyu.

sentences.zh: 保衡才下，諸儒靳薄之，不甚齒，獨呼遘太尉，保衡憾焉。

translations.literal: Baoheng's talent was low; the scholars were stingy and slighted him, not ranking him highly, but alone called Gou Grand Marshal—Baoheng resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Baoheng was mediocre, and the literati held him in low regard, yet they alone addressed Gou as Grand Marshal—a slight Baoheng resented.

sentences.zh: 於是保衡已為相，摭遘罪，繇起居舍人斥播州司馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Baoheng was already chief minister; he gathered Gou's offenses and, from Palace Diary Attendant, expelled him as Military Adjutant of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By then Baoheng was chief minister; he dredged up charges against Gou and banished him from his post as Palace Diary Attendant to military adjutant at distant Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 道三峽，方迫畏不瞑，若有人謂曰：「公無恐，予為公呵禦。

translations.literal: Passing the Three Gorges, he was just then pressed by fear and could not close his eyes, when it seemed someone said: "Sir, do not fear—I will shout and ward off for you."
translations.idiomatic: Traversing the Three Gorges, he was too terrified to sleep when a voice seemed to say, "Do not be afraid, sir—I will guard you."

sentences.zh: 」遘悅悟。

translations.literal: Gou was pleased and understood.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was comforted and at ease.

sentences.zh: 俄謁白帝祠，見帝貌類向所睹，異之。

translations.literal: Soon he visited the shrine of the White Emperor and saw the god's countenance resembled what he had seen before; he marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he visited the White Emperor shrine and found the deity's image matched what he had seen in his vision; he was astonished.

sentences.zh: 未幾，保衡死，召為禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Before long Baoheng died; Gou was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Baoheng died, and Gou was recalled as Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，累擢戶部侍郎、翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: During Qianfu he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Hanlin Academician Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era he rose to Vice Director of Revenue and Expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 僖宗入蜀，以兵部判度支，次綿州，拜同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong entered Shu, Gou, as Minister of War concurrently judging the Treasury, halted at Mian Prefecture and was appointed Associate Chief Minister of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong fled to Shu, Gou—as Minister of War overseeing the treasury—was made chief minister at Mianzhou on the march.

sentences.zh: 始，王鐸主貢舉而得遘，及是，與鐸並位。

translations.literal: At the beginning Wang Duo had presided over the examinations and obtained Gou; now he shared rank with Duo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo had once placed Gou through the examinations; now they served as colleagues.

sentences.zh: 鐸年老，嘗入對踣殿中，遘掖起之。

translations.literal: Duo was old; once entering audience he collapsed in the hall, and Gou raised him by the arm.
translations.idiomatic: Duo was elderly; once he collapsed during audience in the hall, and Gou helped him to his feet.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「遘善事長，大臣和，予之幸也！

translations.literal: The emperor said with pleasure: "Gou is good at serving his elder; the great ministers are in harmony—this is my good fortune!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said gladly, "Gou honors his elder well; harmony among ministers is my good fortune!"

sentences.zh: 」遘曰：「不止以長，乃鐸門生。

translations.literal: Gou said: "It is not only as elder—he is also Duo's disciple."
translations.idiomatic: Gou replied, "It is not only as my elder—he is my teacher."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「鐸選士，朕選宰相，卿無負我！

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Duo selects scholars; I select chief ministers—you must not fail me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Duo chose scholars; I chose chief ministers—do not disappoint me!"

sentences.zh: 」遘頓首謝。

translations.literal: Gou bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Gou kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 從還京師，累拜司空，封楚國公。

translations.literal: Returning with [him] to the capital, he was repeatedly appointed Minister of Works and enfeoffed Duke of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the capital, he was successively made Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Chu.

sentences.zh: 遘負大節，以王佐自任。

translations.literal: Gou bore great integrity and took upon himself the role of royal counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Gou held himself to the highest standards and regarded himself as a counselor to the throne.

sentences.zh: 既當國，風采峭整，天子器之。

translations.literal: Once he held state power, his bearing was sharp and upright, and the Son of Heaven valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in charge of the government, he was stern and commanding in manner, and the emperor held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 時籓鎮多興于盜賊，橫放莫能制，權綱漼弛。

translations.literal: At the time many governorships had risen from bandits; they acted with reckless license and none could control them—the framework of authority was greatly slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Military governors at the time were often men who had risen from banditry; they ran unchecked, and central authority had all but collapsed.

sentences.zh: 支詳在徐州，引散騎常侍李損子凝吉為佐，會牙將時溥逐詳而取節度，溥為饔幹所毒，不死，或讒凝吉為詳報仇者，溥怒殺之。

translations.literal: Zhi Xiang was at Xuzhou and brought in Li Sun's son Ningji, Associate Grand Master of the Palace Retinue, as aide; when the junior officer Shi Bo expelled Xiang and seized the governorship, Bo was poisoned by a kitchen servant but did not die; someone slandered Ningji as one who avenged Xiang, and in anger Bo killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou, Governor Zhi Xiang had taken on Li Sun's son Ningji as his aide. A junior officer, Shi Bo, drove Xiang out and seized the command. Bo was poisoned by a kitchen steward but survived; someone then accused Ningji of plotting revenge on Xiang's behalf, and Bo had him killed in a fury.

sentences.zh: 損時在朝，溥即上言損連謀，請並誅。

translations.literal: Sun was then at court; Bo immediately memorialized that Sun had conspired together and asked that both be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun was at court at the time. Bo immediately reported that Sun had been party to the plot and asked that father and son both be put to death.

sentences.zh: 田令孜受溥金，劾損，付御史獄，中丞盧渥傅成其罪。

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi received Bo's gold, impeached Sun, and handed him over to the censorate prison; Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Wo elaborated and confirmed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi, who had taken bribes from Bo, impeached Sun and had him thrown into the censorate's prison; Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Wo built the case against him.

sentences.zh: 御史王華嫉惡甚，表損不知狀。

translations.literal: Censor Wang Hua hated this bitterly and memorialized that Sun knew nothing of the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wang Hua, outraged, submitted a memorial stating that Sun had no knowledge of the affair.

sentences.zh: 令孜請移神策獄，華不奉詔，奏言：「損近臣，法當死即死，獨不宜取辱於宦人手。

translations.literal: Lingzi requested transfer to the Shence prison; Hua did not obey the edict and memorialized, saying: "Sun is a close minister—if the law says he must die, let him die; only he should not suffer humiliation at eunuch hands."
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi asked that Sun be transferred to the Shence Guard prison. Hua refused and memorialized: "Sun is a close minister of the throne. If the law requires his death, let him die—but not at the hands of eunuchs."

sentences.zh: 」遘即時叩延英爭曰：「凝吉以冤就屠，已不可言。

translations.literal: " Gou immediately went to the Yan Ying Gate and argued, saying: "Ningji was slaughtered though innocent—this already cannot be spoken of."
translations.idiomatic: " Gou went at once to the Yan Ying Gate and protested: "Ningji has been butchered on false charges—that alone is beyond words."

sentences.zh: 損與子音問不接且數期，安得謂同謀哉？

translations.literal: Sun and his son had had no exchange of letters for several periods—how can one say they conspired together?
translations.idiomatic: Sun and his son had not exchanged a word in months—how could they have conspired?

sentences.zh: 溥恃功壞天子法，請案近臣，卑侮王室，有無將之萌。

translations.literal: Bo relies on merit to ruin the Son of Heaven's law; he asks to investigate close ministers, demeans and insults the royal house—there are the first signs of one who lacks restraint toward his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Bo, trading on his military laurels, would trample imperial law, drag a palace minister into his vendetta, and humiliate the throne itself—the seeds of treason are already showing.

sentences.zh: 今損可無罪誅，禍且及臣輩。

translations.literal: If now Sun may be executed without guilt, calamity will reach us ministers as well.
translations.idiomatic: If Sun can be killed without cause, none of us is safe.

sentences.zh: 」帝寤，止免官。

translations.literal: " The emperor came to himself and stopped at dismissal from office only.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor saw reason and halted at stripping Sun of his posts.

sentences.zh: 當此時，令孜持禁軍，權寵可炙，公卿無不附順，唯遘未嘗少下。

translations.literal: At this time Lingzi held the forbidden army; his power and favor were scorching-hot—among ministers none failed to defer, only Gou never lowered himself in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi then commanded the palace armies and burned with power; not one senior official failed to curry favor—only Gou never bowed.

sentences.zh: 後令孜取安邑池鹽給衛軍，王重榮固爭，乃徙重榮它鎮，不受詔。

translations.literal: Later Lingzi took the Anyi salt ponds to supply the guard armies; Wang Chongrong firmly contested this, whereupon [Lingzi] transferred Chongrong to another post; Chongrong did not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lingzi seized the Anyi salt pools for the guard troops. Wang Chongrong objected fiercely; Lingzi then tried to transfer him to another command, but Chongrong refused the order.

sentences.zh: 令孜以兵討之，重榮引沙陀拒王師。

translations.literal: Lingzi used troops to attack him; Chongrong brought in the Shatuo to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi sent troops against him. Chongrong called in the Shatuo Turks to hold off the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 王師敗，逐而西，帝驚，幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: The imperial army was defeated and driven westward; the emperor was alarmed and proceeded to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army was routed and driven west. In alarm, the emperor fled to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 諸節度共劾令孜生事，離間大臣。

translations.literal: The various governors jointly impeached Lingzi for provoking trouble and sowing discord among great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commanders jointly impeached Lingzi for stirring up trouble and driving a wedge among the court's leaders.

sentences.zh: 遘素惡之，與裴澈計，共召硃玫於邠。

translations.literal: Gou had long hated him; with Pei Che he plotted jointly to summon Zhu Mei from Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Gou had long despised Lingzi. He and Pei Che agreed to summon Zhu Mei from Bin.

sentences.zh: 玫起邠兵五千奉迎，與沙陀等連和。

translations.literal: Mei raised five thousand Bin troops to escort and welcome [the emperor], and joined forces with the Shatuo and others.
translations.idiomatic: Mei marched from Bin with five thousand men to escort the emperor, allying with the Shatuo and other forces.

sentences.zh: 令孜迫帝幸陳倉，夜出，百官不及從。

translations.literal: Lingzi forced the emperor to proceed to Chencang; going out by night, the hundred officials could not keep up in following.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzi pressed the emperor to flee to Chencang by night, leaving most of the court behind.

sentences.zh: 玫怒令孜，並望帝不諒其心，謂遘曰：「上奔播六年，中原之人，與賊肝髓流野，得復宗廟，遺老殘民聞輿馬音，流涕相歡。

translations.literal: Mei was angry at Lingzi and also hoped the emperor would not understand his heart; he said to Gou: "The sovereign has wandered in exile six years; the people of the central plains, with bandits, have had liver and marrow flow across the wilds; when we recovered the ancestral temple, leftover elders and broken populace hearing the sound of carriage and horses wept and rejoiced together."
translations.idiomatic: Furious at Lingzi and believing the emperor did not grasp his intentions, Mei said to Gou: "For six years the Son of Heaven wandered in exile. The heartland ran with blood and the fields lay wasted. When we at last restored the ancestral shrines, old survivors wept for joy at the sound of the imperial train."

sentences.zh: 上曾不念，以諸侯勤王功為敕使之寵。

translations.literal: The sovereign never gave it a thought, treating the feudatory lords' merit in aiding the throne as favor for the edict-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the throne thinks nothing of it, rewarding a eunuch envoy for the loyalty of the regional lords.

sentences.zh: 今奸臣為國產怨，我奉命而來，返以為脅君。

translations.literal: Now wicked ministers have bred resentment for the state; I came on command, yet in return am treated as one who threatens the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked men at court have made the realm despise us. We came at imperial summons—and they call us rebels threatening the throne.

sentences.zh: 群臣報國極矣，戰力殫矣，尚能垂頭塌翅求生于黃門哉！

translations.literal: Your ministers have repaid the state to the utmost; battle strength is exhausted—can we yet hang our heads and fold our wings, seeking life at the eunuchs' hands!
translations.idiomatic: We have given everything for the dynasty. Our armies are spent. Must we now crawl before eunuchs to save our skins?

sentences.zh: 喪君有君，公其圖之。

translations.literal: When the ruler is lost there is still a ruler—my lord, consider this.
translations.idiomatic: When one ruler falls, another may rise. You must decide.

sentences.zh: 」遘曰：「上無負天下，顧為令孜掣制，每言必涕數行下。

translations.literal: " Gou said: "The sovereign has not failed the realm; only he is restrained and controlled by Lingzi—each time he speaks tears stream down several lines."
translations.idiomatic: " Gou replied: "The emperor has done no wrong by the realm. He is merely Lingzi's prisoner. He weeps whenever he speaks."

sentences.zh: 陳倉之行，又劫於兵。

translations.literal: The journey to Chencang was again compelled by troops.
translations.idiomatic: The flight to Chencang was another forced march at swordpoint.

sentences.zh: 公誠有憂王室意，宜還籓奉表，請天子復國，策無宜此。

translations.literal: If my lord truly has concern for the royal house, you should return to your frontier post and submit a memorial asking the Son of Heaven to restore the state—no plan is more fitting than this.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly care for the dynasty, return to your command, submit loyal memorials, and ask the emperor to come home. No course is wiser.

sentences.zh: 」玫曰：「諸王才可任天下者不乏。

translations.literal: " Mei said: "Among the princes, those whose talent could undertake the realm are not lacking."
translations.idiomatic: " Mei said, "There is no shortage of princes fit to rule."

sentences.zh: 」遘曰：「人非伊、霍，欲為禍首，未或利也。

translations.literal: " Gou said: "Unless one is Yi Yin or Huo Guang, to wish to be the source of calamity—perhaps nothing is advantageous."
translations.idiomatic: " Gou said, "Unless you are Yi Yin or Huo Guang, leading a coup will profit no one."

sentences.zh: 」玫退曰：「我擇一王為帝，違者斬，尚何事？

translations.literal: " Mei withdrew saying: "I will choose one prince as emperor; whoever disobeys will be beheaded—what else remains to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: " Mei left saying, "I will choose a prince and declare him emperor. Disobey and you die. What more is there to discuss?"

sentences.zh: 」乃立嗣襄王煴，而召遘作冊，遘苦辭，玫更委鄭昌圖，滋恨遘。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enthroned Heir Apparent Prince of Xiang Yun, and summoned Gou to compose the investiture document; Gou bitterly declined; Mei instead entrusted Zheng Changtu, and hated Gou all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " He then enthroned Li Yun, Heir Apparent Prince of Xiang, and ordered Gou to draft the proclamation of accession. Gou refused firmly. Mei turned to Zheng Changtu instead and came to despise Gou.

sentences.zh: 及還長安，使昌圖相煴，罷遘為太子太保。

translations.literal: When they returned to Chang'an, he had Changtu serve as chief minister to Yun, and demoted Gou to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to Chang'an, Mei made Changtu chief minister to the new emperor and stripped Gou of his rank, making him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 移疾不出。

translations.literal: [Gou] feigned illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Gou pleaded illness and refused to leave his house.

sentences.zh: 方其弟蘧為永樂令，往從之。

translations.literal: Just then his younger brother Qu was magistrate of Yongle; [Gou] went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qu was magistrate of Yongle; Gou went to live with him.

sentences.zh: 帝還宮，宰相孔緯與遘雅隙，乃劾嘗為偽臣，即賜死其所，實光啟三年。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the palace, Chief Minister Kong Wei had an old grudge against Gou; he therefore impeached [him] for having once served as minister under the usurpers, and immediately ordered death at his location—in fact Guangqi year 3.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's return, Chief Minister Kong Wei, who bore Gou an old enmity, impeached him for having served the puppet regime and had him executed on the spot. It was Guangqi 3.

sentences.zh: 遘見柄任凡五期，行完而材，逢世多故，召愎臣以濟亂，身汙偽署，不得其死，人為哀之。

translations.literal: Gou was seen in wielding power altogether five times; his conduct was whole and his talent complete; meeting an age of many troubles, he summoned stubborn ministers to relieve disorder; his person was stained by a usurper's appointment; he did not obtain his [proper] death—people mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou held power five times in all—a man of integrity and ability born into chaos. He had turned to hard men to restore order, yet was tainted by service under a puppet emperor and died a shameful death. Many mourned him.

sentences.zh: 瑀曾孫 定

translations.literal: Yu's great-grandson Ding
translations.idiomatic: Yu's great-grandson Ding

sentences.zh: 定，字梅臣，瑀曾孫。

translations.literal: Ding, style name Meichen, was Yu's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Ding, styled Meichen, was Yu's great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 以廕起家陝州參軍事、金城丞。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he began his career as military adjutant of Shan Prefecture and magistrate of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through hereditary privilege as adjutant at Shanzhou and magistrate of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 蒞事清挺。

translations.literal: In conducting affairs he was pure and upright.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was incorruptible and stern.

sentences.zh: 選補黜陟使裴遵慶表為判官，還調萬年主簿。

translations.literal: Personnel selection and promotion-and-demotion commissioner Pei Zunqing recommended him as case officer; on return he was transferred to chief clerk of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing, commissioner for personnel review, recommended him as aide; he was later posted as chief clerk of Wannian County.

sentences.zh: 曆左右司郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as director in the Left and Right Departments of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Left and Right Secretariats.

sentences.zh: 為元載所惡，外遷袁、潤等六州刺史。

translations.literal: Hated by Yuan Zai, he was transferred outward as prefect of six prefectures including Yuan and Run.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai disliked him and had him sent out to serve as prefect of six prefectures, including Yuan and Run.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，有司差天下刺史治最，定與常州蕭復、豪州張鎰為第一，而劭桑稼，均賦稅，業徠遊口，在鎰、復右。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, the relevant office ranked governors nationwide for best administration; Ding together with Xiao Fu of Chang Prefecture and Zhang Yi of Hao Prefecture were first—but in encouraging mulberry and grain, equalizing taxes and levies, and building up the wandering population, he stood above Yi and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era, when the ministry ranked governors for outstanding administration, Ding stood first alongside Xiao Fu of Changzhou and Zhang Yi of Haozhou. Yet in promoting agriculture, equalizing taxes, and settling displaced people, he outranked both.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部侍郎、太常卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 硃泚泚反，詭姓名為張誕，匿裏中，與蔣沇不浼於賊。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, [Ding] disguised his name as Zhang Yan, hid in the countryside, and together with Jiang Yan did not defile themselves before the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Ding assumed the false name Zhang Yan, hid among the people, and—along with Jiang Yan—kept himself unstained by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 事平，擢太子少師。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十七，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-seven; posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：梁蕭氏興江左，實有功在民，厥終無大惡，以浸微而亡，故余祉及其後裔。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Xiao clan of Liang rose in the Jiang-left region and truly had merit among the people; in its end there was no great evil—it perished by gradual decline, and so surplus blessing reached its descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: The Liang Xiao clan rose in the south and truly served the people well. Its end brought no great crime—it faded slowly into oblivion—so fortune lingered on in its descendants.

sentences.zh: 自瑀逮遘，凡八葉宰相，名德相望，與唐盛衰。

translations.literal: From Yu down to Gou, altogether eight generations of chief ministers—fame and virtue succeeding one another, rising and falling with Tang's prosperity and decline.
translations.idiomatic: From Yu to Gou, eight generations produced chief ministers; their renown and virtue tracked the Tang dynasty's rise and fall.

sentences.zh: 世家之盛，古未有也。

translations.literal: The flourishing of this patrician house—since antiquity there has never been its like.
translations.idiomatic: No great family in history ever matched their splendor.
